title: On-device reconstruction-readiness predictor + multi-pass 'add a pass' loop (AUTH #025)
summary: Before upload, compute a cheap on-device reconstruction-readiness score from ARKit signals (coverage, overlap/parallax, blur ratio, light, tracking continuity) and, when it is thin, recommend 'add a quick pass over here' — letting the player append passes to the SAME scan before upload (a multi-pass loop) that merge into one upload bundle. Extends the locked coaching UI (DESIGN_SYSTEM decision 6) and builds on M1-CAPT-01's base capture + gate. Kind, never a hard stop (SPEC §3.1, AUTH #025).

acceptance_tests.test: An on-device readiness score is computed from coverage, overlap/parallax, blur ratio, light, and ARKit tracking continuity; on the corpus a higher score correlates with fewer reconstruction failures (the score is predictive, not cosmetic).
acceptance_tests.evidence: score vs reconstruction-outcome table on the corpus

acceptance_tests.test: When the score is thin, an 'add a pass' prompt points at the weakest region (extends the decision-6 missed-corner arrow) and appending a pass raises coverage on the same scan without restarting; the appended passes merge into one upload bundle (M1-CAPT-01 contract).
acceptance_tests.evidence: clip of the loop + a merged bundle manifest

acceptance_tests.test: The loop never hard-stops: 'Upload anyway' is always available (SPEC §3.1, decision 6c/6e); it reuses the locked coverage-wash + arrow language and respects Reduce Motion (DESIGN_SYSTEM decision 10).
acceptance_tests.evidence: clip of upload-anyway + Reduce Motion on

acceptance_tests.test: On the corpus, first-try reconstruction success is higher with the predictor + multi-pass loop on than off.

history.event: created by the Coordinator as the AUTH #025 follow-up (Owner chose the predictor + multi-pass loop fork).
